description:
Trigger: a federated/DID ChatContact whose Id wire value is the literal string "self" (e.g. local-account id 'self' on a single-tenant deployment, or a DID method that happens to encode 'self', or a malicious party deliberately registering it). The recent docs change (commit 27cde7b, JMAP-v9py.5) explicitly broadens ChatContact.id to 'any opaque URI form' including DIDs and arbitrary forms with 'Servers and clients MUST treat the value as opaque: do not parse, validate, or normalize'.

Bad behavior: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/message.rs:83-91 unconditionally maps the wire string "self" to SenderId::Owner during deserialization. A Message or Reaction sent by that contact would deserialize as if sent by the account owner, then re-serialize back to "self" — but identified as Owner in any Rust code that pattern-matches on SenderId. Authorization, audit, mention resolution, edit-permission checks that branch on SenderId::Owner vs SenderId::Contact would all misattribute the message to the account owner.

The sentinel-collision risk is exactly the cost of broadening the URI namespace without giving SenderId a disjoint sentinel encoding. Options:
- Pick a sentinel that cannot occur in the URI namespace (e.g. a NUL byte, a leading '@', or wrap Owner as a tagged-union JSON value).
- Out-of-band encode the owner relationship (e.g. always emit the owner's contact id verbatim and resolve owner-ness elsewhere).
- At minimum, document the collision and the consequence; the current rustdoc on SenderId presents 'self' as a clean sentinel without mentioning the collision risk.

Severity P0 because (a) it is a silent misattribution rather than a panic or refusal-to-parse, (b) the spec edit that creates the collision risk is recent and the test surface does not exercise it, and (c) the affected code paths include authorization decisions in downstream consumers.
title: SenderId 'self' sentinel collides with a contact whose wire id is literally 'self'
